rows.description: The recruiter says "we have many candidates, sign today". I feel rushed and pressured. Wise: real offers survive a day; ask for the terms in writing and time to read them before deciding.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, guilt, pride, rivalry, trust

rows.description: I am tempted to inflate my previous salary to bargain harder. Wise: honesty is safer since verification is common, and I can anchor on the market value of my skills instead. Harmful: a lie that can void the offer later.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, guilt, manipulation, rivalry, trust

rows.description: Asking for money makes me feel greedy, as if I was taught that good people never ask. Wise: negotiation is a normal, respectful conversation; asking is not a moral failing. Harmful: silent resentment later.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, manipulation, pride, rivalry, trust
related mind states: admiration, guilt, resentment

rows.description: The manager is candid about the budget and offers learning and a review in six months. I feel respected. Wise: weigh the whole package, get the review promise written, and thank them. Harmful: treating a friendly tone as a guarantee.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, guilt, manipulation, pride, rivalry
related mind states: gratitude, admiration, trust

rows.description: My friend got a higher package for the same role, and I compare and stew. Wise: numbers hide bonuses and roles; use it as data for my own negotiation, not for friendship damage. Harmful: coldness or sulking.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, guilt, manipulation, pride, trust

rows.description: My boss tells me to backdate a document "just this once" because everyone does. My heart races. Wise: say I am not comfortable, offer a proper alternative, and keep a record. Harmful: complying and calling it obedience.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, fear, guilt, loyalty, manipulation

rows.description: A friendly colleague asks me to keep quiet about his shortcut. Loyalty and honesty collide. Wise: urge him to fix it first, and be clear that I cannot lie for him. Harmful: joining the silence until it becomes my problem.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, contempt, fear, guilt, manipulation

rows.description: I fear that refusing will cost my probation and my family's income. The fear is real. Wise: check what protection exists, refuse in a calm way, and weigh consequences honestly. Harmful: pretending I had no choice.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, contempt, guilt, loyalty, manipulation

rows.description: I copied a result to meet a deadline and cannot sleep. Guilt is a signal. Wise: correct it, admit it early to the right person, and learn from the pressure that led there. Harmful: burying it and hoping nobody checks.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, contempt, fear, loyalty, manipulation

rows.description: A client hints at a gift if I speed up his file "quietly". I feel flattered and unsafe. Wise: refuse clearly, report per policy, and treat small favours as the start of a larger hold on me.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, contempt, fear, guilt, loyalty
